# `prim_generic_otp` Behavioral Design Specification

## 1. Overview

This module is a generic, simulation/emulation model of a one-time-programmable (OTP) macro wrapper. It emulates the behavior of an OTP storage array and exposes a command interface for initialization, read, and write operations.

The module models:

- A native OTP word storage array.
- Internal ECC protection for stored words.
- One-time-programmable write semantics, including blank checking.
- A sideband test access port.
- Power-sequencing interface behavior.

This module is not an OTP controller. It does not implement partition management, scrambling, digest calculation, or software-visible OTP controller registers.

---

## 2. Parameters

The module is parameterizable with the following configuration:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Native word width | Bit width of one OTP native word. |
| Depth | Number of native words in the OTP storage array. |
| Transfer size width | Width of the transfer-size field. The maximum number of native words transferred in one operation is 2^transfer_size_width. |
| Power sequencing width | Width of the power-sequencing output and input vectors. |
| Test register depth | Number of 32-bit words accessible through the test access port. |
| Memory initialization file | Optional file used to pre-load the emulated OTP storage array. |

The data interface width used for read and write data is:

`maximum transfer size × native word width`

---

## 3. Reset and Initialization

### 3.1 Reset behavior

The module is synchronous and uses an active-low reset. On reset release:

- The module shall enter a pre-initialization state.
- It shall not accept normal read or write commands until an initialization command has been accepted.
- The power-sequencing output shall be all zeros.
- The test access port registers shall be reset to zero.
- The OTP storage array shall not be cleared by reset. Stored contents persist across reset assertion and deassertion.
- The error output shall indicate no error.

### 3.2 Initialization command

After reset, the module shall accept an initialization command. The initialization command shall not depend on the address or write-data values.

Behavior:

- If an initialization command is received before any other command, the module shall perform initialization and return a successful response with no error.
- After initialization completes, the module shall be ready to accept read and write commands.
- If any command other than initialization is presented before initialization, the module shall reject it with a macro error response and remain in the pre-initialization state.
- If an initialization command is presented after the module has already been initialized, it shall be treated as an invalid command and rejected with a macro error response.

---

## 4. Command Interface

### 4.1 Command handshake

The module uses a ready/valid-style command handshake.

- A command is accepted only when the module indicates that it can accept a command and a command request is present.
- The command fields, including command type, address, transfer size, and write data, are sampled when the command is accepted.
- Once a read or write operation is accepted, the module shall not accept another command until that operation has completed and its response has been produced.
- Every accepted command shall produce exactly one response.
- The response channel does not support backpressure. The consuming logic must always be able to accept a response when it is presented.
- Responses are returned in order.

### 4.2 Command types

| Command | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Read | Read one or more native OTP words. |
| Write | Blank-check and then program one or more native OTP words. |
| Init | Initialize the module after reset. |
| Invalid encoding | Any command encoding not defined as read, write, or init. |

Invalid command encodings shall be rejected with a macro error response.

### 4.3 Transfer size and data packing

The transfer-size field encodes the number of native words to transfer, minus one.

For example:

| Transfer-size field value | Number of native words |
|---|---|
| 0 | 1 |
| 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 3 |
| 3 | 4 |

The address selects the first native word to be accessed. Additional words are accessed at consecutive increasing addresses.

For multi-word transfers:

- The least-significant native word on the data bus corresponds to the starting address.
- The next native word occupies the next more-significant bit slice.
- The data bus shall contain all selected native words packed in this order.

The module assumes that a transfer does not wrap around the end of the storage array. A command must not cross the configured depth boundary.

---

## 5. Read Operation

A read command shall read the requested number of native words starting at the supplied address.

The module shall produce a response containing:

- The requested read data, packed according to the transfer-size encoding.
- An error status indicating the result of the read operation.

### 5.1 Read error behavior

- If no ECC error is detected, the response shall indicate no error.
- If a correctable ECC error is detected on one or more of the accessed words, the module shall continue the read operation and the final response shall indicate a correctable ECC error. The data for that word shall still be delivered.
- If an uncorrectable ECC error is detected, the module shall terminate the read operation and return an uncorrectable ECC error response. The response data may be partial; it shall not be assumed to contain the complete requested transfer.

---

## 6. Write Operation

A write command shall program the requested number of native words starting at the supplied address.

OTP storage is modeled as one-time-programmable. A bit that has already been programmed to 1 shall not be cleared to 0.

### 6.1 Blank check

Before performing any write, the module shall perform a blank check on every native word in the requested transfer.

A word passes the blank check if every bit that is already 1 in the current storage word is also 1 in the corresponding write-data word. In other words:

- Writing a 0 to an already-programmed 1 is illegal.
- Writing a 1 to an erased 0 is allowed.
- Writing a 1 to an already-programmed 1 is allowed.

The blank check applies to the native data words. ECC bits are generated internally and are not part of the externally visible data words.

### 6.2 Write response behavior

- If every word in the transfer passes the blank check, the module shall program all requested words and return a successful response with no error.
- If any word fails the blank check, the module shall not write any word in the transfer and shall return a write blank error response.
- If an uncorrectable ECC error is detected during the blank-check read, the module shall abort the write command, shall not write any word, and shall return an uncorrectable ECC error response.
- A correctable ECC error during the blank-check read shall not by itself prevent the write. The write shall proceed if the blank-check condition passes.

The write response shall not include meaningful read data.

---

## 7. Test Access Port

The module shall provide a test access port using the TileLink-UL protocol.

The test port shall provide access to a register file containing a parameterizable number of 32-bit words.

Test port behavior:

- The test registers shall be reset to zero.
- A read access shall return the contents of the addressed test register.
- A write access shall update the addressed test register with the supplied write data.
- Test accesses shall complete successfully without producing error responses.
- The test port shall be independent from the OTP command interface and shall not affect OTP initialization, read, write, or error behavior.

---

## 8. Power-Sequencing Interface

The module shall drive its power-sequencing output to all zeros at all times.

The power-sequencing input is not used by this generic model and shall have no effect on any functional behavior.

---

## 9. Error Codes

The module shall report the following error codes on its error response output:

| Error code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| No error | Operation completed successfully. |
| Macro error | A command was invalid, or the operation could not be completed because of a macro-level malfunction. In this module, this error is used for invalid command encodings and invalid use of the initialization command. |
| Correctable ECC error | A correctable ECC error was detected during a read or blank-check read. |
| Uncorrectable ECC error | An uncorrectable ECC error was detected during a read or blank-check read. |
| Write blank error | A write attempted to clear an already-programmed bit. |

No other error codes shall be generated by this module.

---

## 10. Supported Behavior Summary

| Scenario | Response |
|---|---|
| Reset release | Module waits for initialization. |
| Valid initialization before any other command | Successful initialization response; module becomes ready. |
| Read or write before initialization | Macro error response; module remains uninitialized. |
| Invalid command encoding | Macro error response. |
| Read with no ECC error | Read data returned with no error. |
| Read with correctable ECC error | Read operation completes; response reports correctable ECC error. |
| Read with uncorrectable ECC error | Read operation aborts; response reports uncorrectable ECC error. |
| Write with successful blank check | Words are programmed; successful write response. |
| Write with blank check failure | No word is programmed; write blank error response. |
| Write with uncorrectable ECC error during blank check | No word is programmed; uncorrectable ECC error response. |

---

## 11. Assumptions and Constraints

- The storage array is volatile in the physical sense, but the module shall not clear it on reset. Stored values persist until power is removed.
- Commands must not wrap around the end of the address space.
- The write data for a multi-word transfer must be presented packed in the same order as the read data, with the starting address in the least-significant word position.
- The module models the OTP interface only. It does not provide any scrambling, integrity digest, or partition-locking behavior.
